### Modifications in Each File

1. **`en_txrx.c`**:
   - Added a check to prevent clearing the `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` flag if no polling occurs in the `mlx5e_poll_ico_cq` function. This change helps avoid queueing more Work Queue Entries (WQEs) and prevents overflow of the XSK ICOSQ.

2. **`en.h`**:
   - Introduced a new enumeration value `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` to track the state of pending XSK transmissions.

3. **`tx.c`**:
   - Modified the `mlx5e_xsk_wakeup` function to check and set the `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` flag. If the flag is already set, the function returns early, preventing multiple IRQ triggers for the same wakeup request.

4. **`en_rx.c`**:
   - Changed the return type of the `mlx5e_poll_ico_cq` function from `void` to `int`, allowing it to return a value indicating the number of processed entries. This change is part of the effort to manage the state of the queue more effectively.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the files are interconnected to address the issue of IRQ triggering and potential overflow in the XSK ICOSQ. The introduction of the `MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX` state in `en.h` allows the `mlx5e_xsk_wakeup` function in `tx.c` to manage wakeup requests more effectively by preventing multiple triggers when one is already in progress. The changes in `en_txrx.c` ensure that the state is only cleared when polling occurs, further safeguarding against queue overflows. Lastly, the adjustment in `en_rx.c` to return an integer from `mlx5e_poll_ico_cq` provides feedback on the polling operation, which is crucial for managing the state of the queue and ensuring that the system does not attempt to process more entries than it can handle. Overall, these modifications work together to enhance the robustness of the XSK wakeup mechanism and prevent performance issues related to IRQ handling.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the `mlx5e_trigger_irq` function being called multiple times in quick succession due to the application flooding the driver with wakeup requests. This leads to multiple NOP Work Queue Entries (WQEs) being posted to the XSK ICOSQ, which can overflow the queue and cause performance issues. The lack of a mechanism to prevent additional NOPs from being posted when one is already in progress exacerbates this problem.
        
        Commit message:
        net/mlx5e: Don't trigger IRQ multiple times on XSK wakeup to
 avoid WQ overruns

XSK wakeup function triggers NAPI by posting a NOP WQE to a special XSK
ICOSQ. When the application floods the driver with wakeup requests by
calling sendto() in a certain pattern that ends up in mlx5e_trigger_irq,
the XSK ICOSQ may overflow.

Multiple NOPs are not required and won't accelerate the process, so
avoid posting a second NOP if there is one already on the way. This way
we also avoid increasing the queue size (which might not help anyway).

Fixes: db05815b36cb ("net/mlx5e: Add XSK zero-copy support")
Signed-off-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@mellanox.com>
Reviewed-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@mellanox.com>
Signed-off-by: Saeed Mahameed <saeedm@mellanox.com>  
        
        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c
index fe2d596cb361..3bcdb5b2fc20 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/en/xsk/tx.c
@@ -33,6 +33,9 @@ int mlx5e_xsk_wakeup(struct net_device *dev, u32 qid, u32 flags)
 		if (unlikely(!test_bit(MLX5E_SQ_STATE_ENABLED, &c->xskicosq.state)))
 			return 0;
 
+		if (test_and_set_bit(MLX5E_SQ_STATE_PENDING_XSK_TX, &c->xskicosq.state))
+			return 0;
+
 		spin_lock(&c->xskicosq_lock);
 		mlx5e_trigger_irq(&c->xskicosq);
 		spin_unlock(&c->xskicosq_lock);
